claims.text: An ultrathin ALD-deposited doped-zirconia overlayer will improve low-temperature oxidation on the near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
The overlayer will increase resistance to poisoning by H2O and NO.
The overlayer will enhance catalyst durability under transient and aged automotive-exhaust conditions.
Adding the oxide overlayer will maintain low platinum-group-metal use.
The initial multi-principal-element alloy catalyst has adequately mixed constituent metals.
The initial catalyst has limitations in low-temperature oxidation.
The initial catalyst is susceptible to poisoning.
The initial catalyst degrades over extended use.
A 1–2 nm conformal doped-zirconia or CeO2–ZrO2 overlayer can be deposited by ALD at 100–200 °C.
Fine-tuned ALD parameters will produce a porous 1–2 nm coating.
The intervention will form an intimately interfaced oxide coating with controlled oxygen vacancies.
Oxygen vacancies in the overlayer will promote reactant activation and low-temperature oxidation.
The overlayer will act as a selective barrier that inhibits strong adsorption of poisoning species.
The conformal overlayer will physically protect the alloy surface from structural degradation and thereby preserve catalytic activity.
The treated catalyst will have a lower light-off temperature, with oxidation starting below 150 °C.
The treated catalyst will show reduced sensitivity to H2O and NO relative to the unmodified catalyst.
The treated catalyst will sustain activity better than the unmodified catalyst after accelerated aging.
An overlayer that is too thick or nonporous may impede reactant diffusion and reduce catalytic performance.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions specify a 1–2 nm coating, whereas the structural mediator describes the resulting coating as sub-nanometric.
